Regarding demand for CRE loans, moderate net shares of banks reported weaker demand for 
construction and land development loans and loans secured by nonfarm nonresidential

demand and other banks reported weaker demand for all CRE loan types over the second quarter. 
Meanwhile, a moderate net share of foreign banks reported stronger demand for CRE loans. 
Lending to Households 
(Table 1, questions 13–26) 
Questions on residential real estate lending. Banks reported having left standards basically 
unchanged over the second quarter across all types of residential mortgage loans.9 A modest net 
share of banks reported having tightened standards for HELOCs. 
Meanwhile, banks reported weaker demand, on balance, for most RRE loan categories over the 
second quarter.10 A significant net share of banks reported weaker demand for non-QM non-
jumbo mortgages, and moderate net shares of banks reported weaker demand for subprime, 
government, non-QM jumbo, and QM non-jumbo non-GSE-eligible mortgages. Additionally, a 
modest net share of banks reported weaker demand for GSE-eligible mortgages.11 In contrast, a 
moderate net share of banks reported stronger demand for HELOCs.
